title: Neutrino Pairing Instabilities Require Occupation Number Discontinuities
excerpt: Theoretical modeling shows that neutrino pairing instabilities require occupation number discontinuities, while discretized spectra produce spurious superfluidity.
content:
Theoretical physicists have demonstrated that standard weak interactions among dense astrophysical neutrinos produce pairing instabilities only in the presence of discontinuities in their occupation number. This research examines whether collective interactions in dense astrophysical environments can induce pairing instabilities and reorganize the neutrino momentum distribution, in analogy to the superfluid instability of fermions.

Published in the Journal of High Energy Physics, the open-access theoretical physics study was authored by Damiano F. G. Fiorillo, Georg G. Raffelt, and Günter Sigl. The authors analyzed dense astrophysical conditions where neutrinos behave collectively and exchange flavor through waves of the neutrino plasma, despite the feeble nature of their individual interactions.

The study shows that pairing instabilities under standard weak interactions require sharp distribution discontinuities, such as the sharp Fermi surface responsible for superconductivity in metals.

Additionally, the researchers demonstrated that discretized energy spectra can artificially mimic these occupation discontinuities, falsely generating superfluid instabilities in theoretical calculations. The authors established that these spurious instabilities do not represent physical neutrino-antineutrino superfluidity, because the artificial pairing effects completely disappear when calculations are carried out in the continuum limit.

Subject of Research: Conditions for pairing instabilities and superfluidity in dense astrophysical neutrinos
